plain_description.what: In the merged six-benchmark tree, it compares three rules for routing a new question to a leaf: step-by-step descent from the root, picking the nearest leaf directly ('flat leaf'), or picking the benchmark first. Measured on 6,482 held-out questions.
plain_description.why: Descent through the merged root was losing routing accuracy, and the fix needed to be located.
plain_description.information: It shows which routing rule to use for multi-benchmark runs and where the accuracy loss sits. Result: done, descriptive. Nearest-leaf routing reached 81.6% correct vs 72.1% for descent (+9.5 points, highly significant). Benchmark-first changed almost nothing, so the loss is in the root directions. Nearest-leaf became the recommended default. Later disclosure: about 6.7% of the routed test questions had been visible to the tree's construction, so these numbers carry a contamination caveat (bounded, not re-estimated).
